Description: First external money. Friends/family/angels. $50K-$500K. Validate idea not build product. Use for 6-12 months runway.
Do_This: Use SAFE (YC standard)|Keep it simple — no complex terms|Target 6-12 months runway|Focus on 2-3 angel investors max|Don't overspend — extend runway
Avoid_This: Raising too much too early (dilution regret)|Complex term sheets (use SAFE)|Spending on office/hires before PMF
Key_Documents: YC SAFE agreement|Cap table (Carta/Pulley)|Simple pitch deck (10 slides)

Description: First institutional round. $500K-$3M. Product exists with early traction. Use for PMF validation + first growth. 12-18 months runway.
Do_This: Show early traction (MRR $5K-$25K)|10-15 slide pitch deck|Target 15-20% dilution|Use YC SAFE or priced round|Monthly investor updates after close
Avoid_This: Raising without any traction|Overly optimistic projections|More than 25% dilution|Taking money from wrong investors
Key_Documents: Pitch deck|Financial model (18-month)|Cap table|SAFE or Series Seed docs

Description: Growth round. $3M-$15M. Clear PMF + repeatable growth. Prove unit economics work. Expected: $1M+ ARR with good retention.
Do_This: $1M+ ARR target before raising|Prove unit economics (LTV:CAC > 3:1)|Show retention (GRR > 92%)|Board formation|Detailed 3-5 year financial model
Avoid_This: Raising Series A without PMF|Poor retention hidden by growth|No board governance preparation|Unrealistic projections
Key_Documents: NVCA model docs|Board deck|Financial model (3-5 year)|Data room

Description: 10-15 slides maximum. Tell a story not a data dump. Vision → Problem → Solution → Market → Traction → Team → Ask.
Do_This: Slide order: Vision → Problem → Solution → Market → Traction → Business Model → Team → Financials → Ask|Max 15 slides|Design matters — first impression|Practice 3-min and 10-min versions
Avoid_This: Starting with company history|Too many slides (>15)|Feature dump instead of story|No clear ask amount|Poor design
Key_Documents: 10-15 slide deck (PDF + live)|Appendix with detailed data

Description: 3-5 year projections. First 18 months monthly. Include: revenue, expenses, cash flow, runway. Credible assumptions > hockey stick.
Do_This: Monthly projections for 18 months then annual|Bottom-up revenue model (customers × ARPU)|Include scenarios: base, optimistic, pessimistic|Show path to profitability|Break-even analysis
Avoid_This: Hockey-stick projections without justification|Ignoring customer acquisition costs|Not modeling cash flow|Only showing best case

Description: Monthly investor update. 5-minute read max. Include: highlights, lowlights, KPIs, asks. Build trust through transparency.
Do_This: Send on 1st of each month|Format: Wins → Losses → KPIs → Asks → Thank you|Keep under 5 min read|Share bad news proactively|Specific asks (intros, advice, hiring)
Avoid_This: Only reaching out when you need money|Hiding bad news|No updates for months|Overly long updates

Description: Track all equity ownership from day 1. Know exact dilution at each round. Use Carta or Pulley (free tier). Critical for fundraising.
Do_This: Start tracking day 1|Include: founders + options pool + SAFEs + convertible notes|Model dilution at next round|Keep option pool at 10-20%|Clean cap table = faster fundraising
Avoid_This: Not tracking until fundraising|Spreadsheet errors (use proper tool)|Giving away too much equity early|No option pool reserved
Key_Documents: Cap table on Carta/Pulley|SAFE conversion calculator

Description: Choose revenue model that aligns with how customers get value. Subscription for recurring value. Usage for variable consumption. Transaction for marketplaces.
Do_This: Map value delivery to revenue model|Start simple (1 model)|Validate willingness to pay before building|Consider: how does customer's usage pattern match billing?
Avoid_This: Choosing model because competitors use it|Multiple revenue models too early|Free forever without monetization plan|Usage-based without clear metering

Description: The most important financial decision. Bootstrap = keep control + slower growth. VC = faster growth + dilution + board. Both are valid. Neither is 'better'.
Do_This: Honest self-assessment: do you want to build a unicorn or a profitable business?|Bootstrap if: B2B with proven market, low CAC, fast payback|VC if: network effects, winner-take-all, high capital needs|Hybrid possible: bootstrap first then raise
Avoid_This: Raising VC because it feels prestigious|Bootstrapping if market is winner-take-all|Mixing bootstrap mindset with VC expectations |Taking VC without understanding board dynamics
Amount_Range: Bootstrap: $0 external | VC: depends on stage

Description: Free money that doesn't dilute equity. Government grants (SBIR/STTR), innovation programs, startup competitions. Worth pursuing for deep-tech.
Do_This: Research: SBIR/STTR (US), Horizon Europe (EU), Innovate UK|Apply to startup competitions|Check local government innovation programs|Some cloud credits: AWS Activate, Google for Startups
Avoid_This: Spending more time on grants than product|Grants with restrictive IP terms|Expecting grants to replace revenue|Complex reporting requirements

Description: SaaS revenue recognition: recognize revenue as you deliver the service, not when you receive payment. Critical for accurate financials and fundraising.
Do_This: Recognize subscription revenue monthly (1/12 per month for annual)|Deferred revenue for prepaid annual plans|Separate one-time setup fees from recurring|Align with ASC 606 if applicable
Avoid_This: Recognizing full annual payment as revenue in month 1|Mixing one-time and recurring revenue|Not tracking deferred revenue|Cash-basis accounting for SaaS

Description: Know your industry benchmarks to evaluate performance. Key 2025 SaaS benchmarks: GRR >92%, NRR >110%, LTV:CAC >3:1, Payback <12mo.
Do_This: Compare metrics to stage-appropriate benchmarks|Don't compare seed-stage to Series C benchmarks|Track: MRR growth rate, churn, CAC, LTV, runway|Use OpenView or KeyBanc benchmark reports
Avoid_This: Comparing to unicorn metrics at seed stage|Ignoring benchmarks entirely|Cherry-picking favorable comparisons|Not tracking consistently
